AGENDA
PLANNING COMMISSION
MEETING
Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at (310) 378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
Any person who has made campaign contributions to any of the members of the Planning Commission within twelve months before this meeting, should examine the provisions of Government Code Section 84308 which is posted on the bulletin board outside the Council Chamber.
We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.
The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.

MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  March 15, 2016

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 5:00 p.m. on March 15, 2016, in the City Council Chambers,
340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of Allegiance
followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Absent:  None

Also Present: Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz;
  Assistant City Attorney John Cotti; Julie Cremeans, Minutes Secretary

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

None.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Chair Thomas, upon confirmation the applicants present understood the suggested conditions of
approval, opened the public hearing, confirmed that there were no interested persons wishing to
voice concerns regarding the application considered for the Consent Calendar, and closed the
public hearing.

The Commissioners agreed to move item #8 to the consent calendar.

1.  G-1565-16; Consideration of a Grading Permit Application to install new tee boxes on
  holes #15 & 16, to rebuild the greens on holes #15 & 16, and to modify 16 fairway at the
  Palos Verdes Estates Golf Club located at 3301 Via Campesina. Portion of B, Tract
  4400.

  Applicant:  Palos Verdes Golf Club/Pat Gradoville

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve G-1565-16 for Palos Verdes Estates Golf Club
located at 3301 Via Campesina, , exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided
in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0912 with standard conditions and the following additional
conditions: 1) Grading plans shall be prepared by a licensed landscape architect or civil engineer
and submitted to the City for approval; and 2) The LRP (Legally Responsible Person) shall

Planning Commission  1  March 15, 2016
 obtain coverage under 2009-0009-DWQ (Division of Water Quality) Construction General
Permit and obtain a WDID (Waste Discharge Identification) Number prior to issuance of the
Grading Permit (this requires the preparation of a SWPPP (Stormwater Pollution Prevention
Plan) by a QSD (Qualified SWPPP Developer). The motion was seconded by Commissioner
Welch and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

8.  NC-198R/G-1528R-16; Consideration of revised Neighborhood Compatibility &
  Grading Applications for a new single family residence located at 2700 Via Elevado. Lot
  8, Block 1730, Tract 7540. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Pao & Yu Kuo

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve NC-198R/G-1528R-16 for 2700 Via Elevado,
exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-
0911 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) A licensed survey of
the floor area and building height shall be completed and submitted to the City to verify
compliance with the approved floor area and building height for the subject lot; 2) The project
creates, adds or replaces more than 10,000 square feet of impervious surface and portions of the
lot being graded/excavated exceed 25% grade; thus, the project shall comply with the City’s
municipal NPDES permit and requirements set forth in Municipal Code 13.08.060, Section C;
and 3) Remove the parking pad southeast of the driveway and construct a new Hollywood berm
per City Standard ST-30 with landscaping behind. The motion was seconded by Commissioner
Welch and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

PUBLIC HEARING

2.  Planning Commission Resolution PCR-2016-0914 recommending the City Council
  amend Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code Title 17 (Zoning procedures) and Title 18
  (Zoning regulations) regarding short term or vacation rentals in residential areas.

Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman introduced the application, per written material.

Chair Thomas inquired about time restraints, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman explained a
pending bill that would require operators of websites to respect local regulations.

Commissioner Evans asked about current short-term rental activity, and Planning Director Repp-
Loadsman responded that 15 rental sites have been identified.

Commissioners Kao and Welch and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman discussed complaints
from neighbors, occupancy tax and whether other cities have passed regulations.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  2  March 15, 2016
 Elizabeth and Lewy Kallas (1328 Via Margarita), Karen Logan (2760 Via Anita), Patricia
Maiolo (1645 Via Arriba), Randy Aguirrie (2921 Palos Verdes Drive North), Drexel Chapman
(608 Via Bodega), Jin Anastassiou (604 Paseo Del Mar), Marsha Davis (1744 Addison Road),
Kathryn Chapman (608 Via Bodega) and Ried Schott (1632 Via Lazo) all came forward in
opposition to short-term rentals due to loss of privacy and security, traffic and parking issues,
decreased property values, neighborhood culture changes, lack of transparency, hotel revenue
loss, lack of benefit to neighbors, criminal activity, incompatibility with city goals, suspicious
activity, regulation issues, penalties, tax increases and residential zoning.

Frank Overbeek (1329 Via Margarita) came forward as a rental owner in favor of short-term
rentals, citing false complaints, sufficient regulations, rights of property owners, no zoning
changes, costly regulation and enforcement with no benefit.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Welch commented that he is pleased with the process, reminded everyone about
the workshop that was held and proposed a total ban on this proposal.

Commissioner Kao agreed and discussed why regulations would be impossible to enforce.

Commissioner Evans also agreed and discussed reserving the character of Palos Verdes Estates.

Chair Thomas and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman discussed the Planning Commission’s
ability to make policy, and Chair Thomas went on to discuss regulations and enforcement.

Chair Thomas and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman agreed to re-open the public hearing at a
future meeting to discuss prohibitive language on this proposal.

CONTINUED TO THE APRIL 19, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

OLD BUSINESS

3.  M-1067-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3819 Via La
  Selva. Portion of Lot T, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Javier & Jenna Martinez
  4733 Torrance Blvd., #121
  Torrance, CA 90503

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louie Tomaro (architect at 2617 N. Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward and
presented the application.

Planning Commission  3  March 15, 2016
 The Commissioners and Mr. Tomaro discussed various design elements.

Tom Funk (3925 Via Picaposte) came forward in opposition to the application, citing a 5-foot
elevation change and asking that the Planning Commission reverse it.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and advised that the back yard was not raised 5 feet.

Commissioners Kao and Evans and Mr. Tomaro discussed the elevation and landscaping.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioners Kao, Evans, Welch and Hunter and Chair Thomas discussed the pool structure
height and the adjacent neighbor’s fence height. They all agreed that they could not support this
project.

Commissioner Kao commented that he thought the Commission had previously pointed out
concerns about the mass of the pool house, but the elevation has not gone down and impacts to
the Funks remains the same.

Commissioner Evans agreed and pointed out that it has been four meetings with Mr. Funk
talking about the impacts to his privacy and openness.

Commissioner Welch discussed the continued increase in height.

Commissioner Hunter also commented that this is the fourth time with the same consistent
direction every time and no material change.

Chair Thomas commented that he was uncomfortable with the project when it was first approved
and doesn’t want to exacerbate the impact to the Funk residence.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to deny M-1067-15 for 3819 Via La Selva. The motion
was seconded by Commissioner Kao and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

4.  NC-1546/G-1561/M-1078-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading &
  Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 960 Paseo La
  Cresta. Lot 9, Tract 31329. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Prolina LLC
  2301 Via Acalones
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Planning Commission  4  March 15, 2016
 Commissioners Kao and Hunter and City Planner Corpuz discussed building height and fence
height.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louie Tomaro (architect at 2617 N. Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward and
presented the application.

Chingmuh Lee (956 Paseo La Cresta), Todd and Lydia Bauer (959 Paseo La Cresta) and Morris
Asch (949 Paseo La Cresta) all came forward in opposition to this project citing ridge height,
chimney height, chimney type, preservation of the queen’s necklace view, obstructive
landscaping and neighborhood compatibility guidelines.

Brad Dudley (345 Third Street, Laguna Beach) came forward in opposition as the architect for
the Bauers and commented that there has been progress made on massing and floor area
allocation, but there is still a view impact, and Mr. Dudley proposed solutions to reduce the
impact.

Samantha Lamberg (21515 Hawthorne Boulevard, Torrance) came forward in opposition to the
project, discussed legal issues raised in a letter presented by Albro Lundy and suggested that
views are not protected in Palos Verdes Estates. Ms. Lamberg discussed CC&Rs and ordinances
that identify protection of views and added that this is a large lot with many opportunities to
design the structure with no impacts on neighboring views and that the plate heights can easily
be reduced.

Albro Lundy (1701 Via Arriba) came forward representing the owners and discussed
concessions made by the architect. Mr. Lundy stated that there is no view ordinance, that the
neighbors are requesting less of a house than what is already there, that all the homes in the area
are well above the height of this home and that the Commission should look at compatibility, not
disapproval from neighbors. Mr. Lundy added that the applicant could have gone up instead of
putting a floor underground, that the “significant impacts” have to be from the main viewing area
of a home and that the view impact is reasonably practicable.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and discussed the tennis court views, ocean views, plate heights,
chimneys, the preservation of one view and enhancement of another, ridge heights and
neighboring chimneys. Mr. Tomaro also pointed out that a reasonable application was presented,
and further adjustments were made for the neighbors.

Commissioner Kao and Mr. Tomaro discussed the queen’s necklace views and ridge height.

Chair Thomas and Mr. Tomaro discussed fencing types and landscaping plans.

Commissioner Evans and Mr. Tomaro discussed plate heights, with Mr. Tomaro pointing out
that because the application digs down plate heights aren’t relevant and going down further
would not be reasonable.

Commissioner Hunter and Mr. Tomaro further discussed ridge height.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  5  March 15, 2016
 Commissioner Kao acknowledged the concessions made by the architect but expressed his
concerned for the view impact to the Lees and suggested reducing the height by 14 inches.

Commissioner Evans agreed that revisions should be made.

Commissioner Welch stated that he could approve this project as submitted but is confused how
the Lee house could have been built, given the impact it had on the Asch house, per CC&Rs.

Commissioner Hunter commended the applicant and agreed with Commissioners Kao and Evans
in regard to the height.

Chair Thomas agreed with Commissioner Welch and pointed out the sacrifices that the home
owners have made. It’s important to look at the broader context of this application, as it could be
more monotheistic on existing grade, and there are some impacts but they have been mitigated to
a reasonable and practicable extent. Vegetation should be maintained to preserve the views, and
the chimneys are within the profile of the ridgeline, but the applicant made more than reasonable
strides to mitigate impacts.

Commissioner Hunter and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman discussed the tree trimming
ordinance, and Chair Thomas discussed imposing vegetation conditions.

Commissioner Hunter and Chair Thomas discussed the importance of the queen’s necklace view,
with Commissioner Hunter agreeing that with a 12-inch reduction he could approve.

Commissioner Evans commented that what’s proposed is outstanding and questioned why the
extra foot is not easy to do.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and offered to either lower the structure 6 inches or lower the ridge to
the same height as the existing ridge, which would be approximately 1 foot, and Chair Thomas
and Commissioners Hunter, Kao and Evans all discussed the proposed options, and the
Commission and Staff discussed maintenance of vegetation.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-1546/G-1561/M-1078-15 for 960 Paseo La
Cresta, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2015-0893 with standard conditions. and the following additional conditions: 1) All non-
standard encroachments shall be removed including, but not limited to, the stepping stones
within the City right-of-way; 2) The project creates, adds or replaces more than 10,000 square
feet of impervious surface and portions of the lot being graded/excavated exceed 25% grade;
thus, the project shall comply with the City’s municipal NPDES permit and requirements set
forth in Municipal Code 13.08.060, Section C; 3) A geotechnical report shall be provided that
supports the proposed construction of structures, walls, and a pool and shall include a
determination that the development will not adversely surcharge or otherwise impact the existing
sewer line; 4) Landscaping between the side yard setback line and the westerly property line
shall not exceed 36-inches; and 5) The east-west ridgeline, west of the front entry shall be
reduced to an elevation of 662.38.5. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was
carried by unanimous oral vote

Planning Commission  6  March 15, 2016
 5.  NC-1551/M-1084/M-1085-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility &
  Miscellaneous Applications for additions and remodeling to the single family residence
  located at 1417 Via Zumaya. Lot 68, Tract 27438. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tom Wooge
  3307 Johnston Ave.
  Redondo Beach, CA 90278

  Owner:  Chuanjie Zhou

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Tom Wooge (architect at 3307 Johnston Avenue, Redondo Beach) came forward and presented
the application.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Roger Chen (1413 Via Zumaya) came forward in opposition and asked for a sectional study of
the new addition in relation to the retaining wall and discussed worst case scenario and steep
grade. Mr. Chen pointed out that the foundation will have to be deeper into the earth and that the
garage will be close to the street.

Karna Gottdener (1420 Via Galicia) also came forward in opposition and discussed the
neighborhood compatibility ordinance, homes built before the ordinance was established, the
absence of parkland and the extension butting up to the setback with eaves extending into the
setback and asked that the Commission regulate the feeling of crowding and maintain the
neighborhood character.

Mr. Wooge re-approached and addressed the concerns that were raised, pointing out that this
house has one of the largest setbacks and explaining the flagging and overhang.

Chair Thomas, Commissioners Hunter and Evans and Mr. Wooge discussed driveway length, the
trash area, the garage floor height and the ridge height.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Chair Thomas commented that he mainly wanted to review the impact of the balconies to the
adjacent neighbors and that he is satisfied that the garage meets his requirements for minimizing
impact on the neighborhood, several properties had short driveways and this one wouldn’t be out
of character for the neighborhood, this structure is visible above the neighbor’s pool deck but
doesn’t create an unreasonable impact, the rear deck is substantial and could be concerning for
privacy but there is a significant downhill slope that will require creativity to have an outdoor
living area and what’s proposed is reasonable.

Commissioner Evans expressed his concern with the architect not meeting with the impacted
neighbors as a matter of process.

Commissioner Welch expressed his concern with the structural support for the garage, and
Planning Director Repp-Loadsman confirmed that the City relies on building officials and

Planning Commission  7  March 15, 2016
 engineers to ensure buildings are properly designed and constructed. Commissioner Welch then
commented that his concerns have been mitigated appropriately.

Commissioner Kao noted the neighbors’ comments on traffic safety considerations.

Commissioner Hunter expressed his concern with the trash area and suggested the other side of
the garage where a big platform area within the setback wouldn’t be required. Mr. Wooge re-
approached and proposed moving them inside the garage with a smaller pad to remove the trash.
Chair Thomas commented that he’s not troubled by it and doesn’t perceive an impact.

Commissioner Evans commented that he would agree with the majority.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-1551/M-1084/M-1085-15 for 1417 Via
Zumaya, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2016-0902 with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans
and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

NEW BUSINESS

6.  CDP-90R/WT-121R-16; Revised Coastal Development Permit and Wireless
  Telecommunication Facilities Applications to modify an existing facility within the City
  right-of-way across from 1009 Palos Verdes Drive West.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Michael Shonafelt (attorney for Crown Castle, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application, pointing out that this is critical telephone infrastructure for phone
and data service, both in terms of coverage and capacity, including 9-1-1 calls, as more residents
are dropping their traditional telephone service.

Commissioners Evans and Kao and Mr. Shonafelt discussed the signal strength for this tower
contributing to the overall architecture and how the box can be so far away and function well.

Ken White (1120 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward and commented that the towers are in
his view; the antenna that is up now works quite well and is hardly noticeable, he is unaware of
the need for a new larger pole and antenna at this location, and the neighborhood paid for
undergrounding in the 1960s and doesn’t want to see what looks like a telephone pole there now.

Mr. Shonafelt re-approached and explained that the technologies are changing by the day and
data demands are placing increasing burdens on existing infrastructure and that broadband
coverage has fallen dramatically.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  8  March 15, 2016
 Commissioners Hunter and Kao commented that they are ready to approve.

Commissioner Evans asked for the consultant’s view on why there is a need for a new larger
pole and antenna at this location, and Jonathan Kramer (2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles)
came forward as the technical consultant for the City and explained that the purpose is to extend
the coverage and that a significant portion of the signal is not being utilized. This aims the signal
more up and down the street, as opposed to being wasted into the hillside and toward the ocean.

Commissioner Welch commented that he should get better service and is ready to approve.

Chair Thomas commented that this is consistent with others that are being approved and he
would like to improve service on the hill.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve CDP-90R/WT-121R-16 for the City right-of-
way across from 1009 Palos Verdes Drive West, exempt from CEQA and subject to the
conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0907 with standard conditions and the
following additional conditions: 1) The steel pole shall be burnished prior to painting. The pole
and all equipment mounted on it (including without limitation to the antennas, antenna mounting
hardware, and cables) must be painted a flat brown, and maintained in the same condition
thereafter; 2) The replacement steel pole is not a wireless tower for any purpose, but rather it is
considered only a replacement City street sign pole which shall remain as City-owned; 3)
Permittee shall place its name on the recommended power meter; 4) Permittee shall install and
at all times maintain in good condition an “RF Notice” and “Network Operations Center
Information” sign on the steel pole at approximately 13.8 feet AGL; 5) Permittee shall ensure
that all RF signage complies with FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2 for color, symbol, and
content conventions; 6) Attached traffic signs shall be installed in accordance with the MUTCD
(Manual Uniform Traffic Control Devices) California Edition; and 7) Attached traffic signs shall
be with approved hardware per the City’s Maintenance Foreman. The motion was seconded by
Commissioner Welch and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

7.  WT-142-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way across from 3912 Palos Verdes Drive North.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618u

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Kao asked about moving the DAS node to be lower or higher with the bus stop,
and Jonathan Kramer (2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles) came forward as the technical
consultant for the City and responded that the issue of radiofrequency safety at 14 feet or 17 feet
would comply with FCC rules.

Commissioner Evans asked whether Mr. Kramer has considered whether the pole could be
moved, and Mr. Kramer responded that the purpose is to calibrate, and Crown Castle will replace
the existing bus stop pole, which would become City owned.

Planning Commission  9  March 15, 2016
 CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Michael Shonafelt (attorney for Crown Castle, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application and incorporated comments from the last agenda item.

David Bray (3901 Palos Verdes Drive North) came forward in opposition of the application,
stating that this location is intrusive, kids congregate in the area every morning for school and
play around that pole, this could be harmful to children, there are radiofrequency concerns, this is
the most noticeable part of Palos Verdes Estate and is an eyesore, a less intrusive location should
